segments.t: Asian markets plunge as investors rush out of AI stocks.
South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index lost over 8% on Monday, tripping circuit breakers as
chip makers SK Hynix and Samsung tumbled. A sell-off in AI stocks started last week
on Wall Street after disappointing results from Broadcom. On Friday, the Philadelphia
Semiconductor Index lost 10%. So is this a healthy pause or the start of a correction?
Janet Morey is head of market analysis at RBC Bruin Dolphin. Janet Money has surged
into chip makers lately, especially the two Korean giants. Were those valuations just overstretched?
I think valuations still look pretty decent for the Korean chip makers now. I mean, their
forwards price to earnings ratio are below 10. I mean, there is a huge debate over whether
the increasing demand for memory chips is cyclical or is actually a supercycle. So if
it is a supercycle, then there is plenty of room for these valuations to be rerated higher
in the future. But of course, I think from decades of experience, many investors also
worry that it could still be a cyclical in nature. So I guess given that the South Korean
chip makers have basically rallied multiple times over the past year or so, I think this
brief pause or break is actually quite healthy. You don't think then that this is a sign of
a broader loss of faith in the AI trade with valuations as high as they are? I don't
think so. I think we all know that AI is a multi-year trend. It is becoming more and
more useful and we see larger and broader deployment of AI across many industries and
it is really just the beginning. And we also still continuously see hundreds of billions
of dollars being invested in the space and there is no sign of that.
